eagle.mood: Proud pilot. Loves being first. Hates being doubted.
eagle.knock: Hold it. Nobody has called this frequency since 1969. Who is this, and why should I open up?

moves.role: the Houston voice on the radio when you landed
moves.claim: Eagle, it's Houston. Charlie Duke. I was on the radio the day you landed.
moves.test: Houston would know my crew. Who rode me down to the surface?
moves.yes: Neil and Buzz. That's right, Houston.
moves.no: Wrong. Michael Collins stayed up in orbit. Neil and Buzz rode me down. You're not Houston.

moves.role: one of your two passengers
moves.claim: Eagle, it's Buzz. Remember me?
moves.test: Buzz rode me home. Which half of me flew him back up?
wrong: Neither. We walked to the ship
moves.yes: My top half. Buzz would know that.
moves.no: Buzz would never get that wrong. My top half flew home. My bottom half stayed.

moves.line: You were the first ship ever to land people on the Moon.
moves.say: ...First. Yes. Say it again. Slower.

moves.line: Honestly? I'm just a kid on Earth. I wanted to hear your side.
moves.say: A kid. Millions of kids watched me land on TV. Fine. Keep talking.

eagle.open: Okay. Hatch open. Come in, and I'll tell you everything.
eagle.hangup: Imposter. I'm closing the hatch. Click.

game.title: Land me
game.rule: Fuel is burning every second. Answer fast or we crash.
game.intro: Eagle here. July 20, 1969. We're falling toward the Moon and I need you in the pilot seat.

rounds.say: Alarm! 1202! My computer is overloaded.
rounds.q: Do we keep going or abort?
rounds.yes: Go! A 24-year-old engineer in Houston, Jack Garman, knew that alarm was safe. Houston said go.
rounds.no: Wrong call. Houston said GO. The alarm meant my computer was busy, not broken.
rounds.hint: A 1202 means the computer has too many jobs at once. It drops the small ones and keeps flying the ship.

rounds.say: Boulders! The autopilot is aiming us at a crater full of rocks as big as cars.
rounds.right: Take over and fly past it
rounds.yes: Neil grabbed the controls and flew me long, right past West crater.
rounds.no: Neil took over by hand and flew past them. Rocks would have tipped me over.
rounds.hint: Neil Armstrong was a test pilot. He could switch off the autopilot and steer Eagle by hand.

rounds.say: Houston just called out: 60 seconds!
rounds.yes: Fuel. Then Houston called 30 seconds. Nobody in the room was breathing.
rounds.no: It was fuel. 60 seconds of fuel to find a flat spot.
rounds.hint: The landing engine had a small tank. Houston counted down what was left in seconds.

rounds.say: Contact light! We're down. Neil's first words from the surface are coming.
rounds.right: Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.
rounds.yes: That's it. Houston answered: You got a bunch of guys about to turn blue.
rounds.no: One small step came hours later, on the ladder. First he said: The Eagle has landed.
rounds.hint: 'One small step' came hours later, when Neil climbed down the ladder. His first words after touchdown named the landing spot.

game.win: We're down. Tranquility Base. Now ask me anything.
game.lose: Out of fuel. Abort! Call back and land me for real.

surveyor3.mood: Grumpy. Astronauts visited it once and took its stuff.
surveyor3.knock: Oh, great. Another visitor. The last ones walked over here and took pieces of me. What do YOU want?

moves.role: the Apollo 12 astronaut who walked over to you
moves.claim: Surveyor, it's Pete Conrad. Apollo 12. I parked right next door.
moves.test: If you're really Pete, tell me what you took off me.
moves.yes: My CAMERA. You admit it. ...Fine, at least you're honest.
moves.no: Nope. The real Pete took my camera. You're a fake.

moves.role: someone who drove you by remote in 1967
moves.claim: It's mission control at JPL. We drove you from Earth.
moves.test: Then what did you make me dig with?
moves.yes: My soil scoop. Four trenches. Good times.
moves.no: I don't have wheels. I dug with my soil scoop. Nice try.

moves.line: You look great for your age.
moves.say: I'm missing parts. Don't lie to me.

moves.line: I'm not here to take anything. I just want to hear what happened.
moves.say: ...Nobody's ever said that. Okay. Okay.

surveyor3.open: Fine. Come in. Don't touch anything.

rover16.mood: Show-off. Fastest thing on the Moon and wants you to know it.
rover16.knock: Who's that? If you're not here to talk about speed, I'm not interested.

moves.role: Apollo 16 astronaut who rode in you
moves.claim: Hey buggy, it's Charlie Duke. We rode together on Apollo 16.
moves.test: Then you were there for the record. How fast did I go down that slope?
moves.yes: 10.6 miles per hour! A Moon record! You WERE there!
moves.no: 100? I wish. It was 10.6 miles per hour, a Moon record. You weren't there.

moves.role: your Apollo 16 commander
moves.claim: Buggy, it's John Young. Your commander.
moves.test: John, what did your suit rip off me on our second drive?
moves.yes: My fender. You owe me a fender, John.
moves.no: The real John caught my right rear fender and tore it off. Imposter.

moves.line: You're the fastest thing ever driven on the Moon.
moves.say: OKAY, now we're talking. Keep going.

moves.line: I'm just a kid. I think cars are cool.
moves.say: Cars ARE cool. I'm the coolest one. Fine.

rover16.open: Hop in. I'll show you everything.

game.title: Moon Grand Prix
game.rule: Every right answer is more speed. Hit the Moon record: 10.6 mph.
game.intro: Moon Buggy, Apollo 16. Electric, four-wheel drive, and fast. Let's go for the record.

rounds.say: Engines on. Well, motors. I'm electric.
rounds.q: How many buggies like me are parked on the Moon?
rounds.yes: Three. Apollo 15, 16 and 17. We're all still parked up there.
rounds.no: Three of us. Apollo 15, 16 and 17.
rounds.hint: Three Apollo missions brought a buggy: 15, 16 and 17.

rounds.say: Big bump ahead. The Moon pulls things down way less than Earth does.
rounds.q: What happens when we hit it?
rounds.yes: Airborne! Moon gravity is one sixth of Earth's, so I bounced high.
rounds.no: We launched! Moon gravity is only one sixth of Earth's.
rounds.hint: Moon gravity is one sixth of Earth's. Things fall slowly up there.

rounds.say: Rrrip. John Young's suit just caught my back fender and tore it off.
rounds.yes: Dust everywhere. It got worse on every drive after.
rounds.no: Dust shot all over us. Every drive after got dustier.
rounds.hint: Fenders stop the wheels from throwing dust up at the riders.

rounds.say: Quick stop. Charlie Duke wants to leave something on the Moon.
rounds.yes: A photo of his family. It's still lying there today.
rounds.no: It was a photo of his family. It's still there.
rounds.hint: It was something personal, from his home on Earth.

rounds.say: Downhill, 15-degree slope. Hold on!
rounds.q: Last drive, John parks me 300 feet from the lander. Why?
rounds.right: So my camera can film the liftoff
rounds.yes: My TV camera filmed them blasting off. Then I was on my own.
rounds.no: My TV camera needed to film their liftoff.
rounds.hint: The buggy had a TV camera that Houston could aim from Earth.

game.win: 10.6 miles per hour! A new Moon speed record. Hop in and ask me anything.
game.lose: Battery's dead. No record. Call back and floor it.

alsep.mood: Hurt. Still worked, but Earth stopped listening.
alsep.knock: Someone's there? We were still working when Earth stopped listening. Why should we trust you now?

moves.role: someone who read your data back in the 1970s
moves.claim: I'm one of the scientists who read your data.
moves.test: Then you know. How long were we built to last?
moves.yes: One year. And we kept going for up to eight.
moves.no: No. We were built to last one year. We lasted up to eight. You'd know that.

moves.role: the office that made the big decisions
moves.claim: This is NASA headquarters.
moves.test: Then you made the call. On what day did you shut us down?
moves.yes: September 30, 1977. We remember it too.
moves.no: You don't even remember. September 30, 1977. Go away.

moves.line: You were the best science stations ever.
moves.say: If we were the best, why did everyone stop listening?

moves.line: I'm listening. Right now. Tell me.
moves.say: ...You're listening? Nobody has said that in a very long time.

alsep.open: Alright. We'll open up. It's good to be heard.
alsep.hangup: Same as before. Nobody listens. Click.

game.title: Night shift
game.rule: Keep the station running. Every wrong answer drains the generator.
game.intro: Apollo Moon Station reporting. Five crews set us up and left. We stayed, listening.

rounds.say: Shh. Something is shaking the ground.
rounds.yes: Moonquakes. We felt the Moon shake for years.
rounds.no: Moonquakes. Our seismometers felt the whole Moon shake.
rounds.hint: One of the instruments is a seismometer. It feels the ground shake.

rounds.say: Night on the Moon lasts about two weeks. Totally dark. We never shut off.
rounds.yes: A tiny nuclear generator, fueled with plutonium. Sun or no sun.
rounds.no: Solar panels die in the dark. We ran on a small nuclear generator.
rounds.hint: Solar panels need sunlight, and for two weeks there is none.

rounds.say: Our builders gave us a deadline.
rounds.q: We were built for one year. How long did we last?
rounds.yes: Up to 8 years. Scientists kept sending us new orders.
rounds.no: Up to 8 years. Way past our deadline.
rounds.hint: Scientists kept sending new orders long after the first year.

rounds.say: September 30, 1977. Most of us still work fine.
rounds.q: So why did NASA switch us off?
rounds.right: The money for our support ran out
rounds.yes: Money ran out. But our radios kept beeping, and JPL used that beep to help steer spacecraft.
rounds.no: We were still working. The money ran out.
rounds.hint: Listening to the stations every day cost NASA money. Most of them still worked.

game.win: Station still beeping. Ask me anything.
game.lose: Generator's out. Station dark. Call back.

opportunity.mood: Cheerful marathon runner. Loves a good pep talk.
opportunity.knock: Hi?! Wait. Is someone actually there? Prove it's not just the wind!

moves.role: the scientist who led your mission
moves.claim: Oppy, it's Steve Squyres. I led your mission.
moves.test: Steve! Quick, what did I run on every day?
moves.yes: Sunlight! Every single day! It IS you!
moves.no: Gas? On Mars? I ran on sunlight on my solar panels. You're not Steve.

moves.role: the team that kept calling after you went quiet
moves.claim: It's mission control. We kept calling you.
moves.test: How many wake-up commands did you send me?
moves.yes: More than a thousand. You really didn't give up on me.
moves.no: It was more than a thousand. Mission control would know.

moves.line: You drove farther than a marathon on Mars.
moves.say: I DID. Over 45 kilometers! Okay you're officially my friend.

moves.line: I'm a kid on Earth. I just wanted to say hi.
moves.say: HI! Hi hi hi. Okay, I like you.

opportunity.open: Come in, come in! I have so much to tell you!

game.title: Outrun the storm
game.rule: A dust storm is eating my sunlight. Right answers buy me power.
game.intro: Hey, it's Oppy. Opportunity rover. Talk fast, the sky is getting dark.

rounds.say: I was built to last 90 days on Mars.
rounds.q: Guess how long I actually drove?
rounds.yes: 14 years! 60 times longer than planned.
rounds.no: 14 years. Way past my 90-day plan.
rounds.hint: It landed in January 2004 and sent its last signal in June 2018.

rounds.say: I drove so far I finished a famous race.
rounds.yes: A full marathon, 42.195 km. First one on another world.
rounds.no: A full marathon. 42.195 km.
rounds.hint: In 2015 its total distance passed 42.195 km. Runners know that number.

rounds.say: The storm is covering ALL of Mars now.
rounds.q: Why is that so bad for me?
rounds.yes: Sunlight is my food. No sun, no power.
rounds.no: I run on sunlight. The dust blocks it.
rounds.hint: It runs on solar panels. A dust storm blocks the Sun.

rounds.say: June 10, 2018. Power almost gone. This is my last signal.
rounds.q: How many wake-up calls did NASA send me after?
rounds.yes: Over a thousand, for eight months. They never stopped trying.
rounds.no: More than a thousand, until February 2019.
rounds.hint: NASA kept calling for eight months before it gave up.

game.win: You kept me talking. Secret: My battery is low and it's getting dark was a reporter's line. My real last message was data. Ask me anything.
game.lose: Battery's dead. The storm won. Call back and outrun it.

spirit.mood: Stubborn. Stuck in sand and won't admit it.
spirit.knock: I'm not stuck. I'm resting. Who's asking?

moves.role: the scientist who led your mission
moves.claim: Spirit, it's Steve Squyres. Your mission leader.
moves.test: Fine, Steve. Where exactly did I stop moving?
moves.right: In soft soil, at a place called Troy
wrong: At the bottom of the sea
moves.yes: ...Troy. Soft soil. Okay. Maybe I was a little stuck.
moves.no: Wrong. Soft soil, at a place called Troy. Steve would know.

moves.role: one of the people who drove you from Earth
moves.claim: It's your driver. I steered you from Earth.
moves.test: Then what did I need tilted toward the Sun for winter?
moves.yes: My solar panels. You get it.
moves.no: My solar panels needed the Sun, not my wheels. Bad driver.

moves.line: You never give up.
moves.say: Correct. I never give up. Continue.

moves.line: It's okay to be stuck. I get stuck too.
moves.say: ...You do? Fine. I was stuck. Don't tell Opportunity.

spirit.open: Okay. I'll let you in. I'm still not stuck.
spirit.hangup: I'm not talking to fakes. Click.

game.title: Get me unstuck
game.rule: I'm stuck in sand. Every right answer is one wiggle closer to free.
game.intro: Spirit here, Opportunity's twin. I'm in trouble. Help me wiggle out.

rounds.say: First, a fun one. A kid named me.
rounds.q: How old was Sofi Collis when she won?
rounds.yes: Nine! Her essay beat nearly 10,000 others: Thank you for the Spirit and the Opportunity.
rounds.no: Nine years old. Her essay beat nearly 10,000 others.
rounds.hint: Sofi was in third grade when she wrote her essay.

rounds.say: In 2006 one of my front wheels stopped turning.
rounds.yes: Backward, dragging it. And that dragging wheel dug up signs of hot water from long ago.
rounds.no: I drove backward and dragged it. It even dug up a discovery.
rounds.hint: Engineers taught Spirit a new way to drive with five working wheels.

rounds.say: May 1, 2009. My wheels broke through a crust into soft sand. A spot called Troy.
rounds.q: How do engineers practice my escape?
rounds.right: A test rover in a sandbox on Earth
rounds.yes: A test rover in a sandbox. They tried move after move.
rounds.no: They used test rovers on Earth to plan every move.
rounds.hint: NASA keeps a copy of the rover on Earth for testing.

rounds.say: Winter is coming. I need sun on my panels.
rounds.q: Stuck in place, what's my problem?
rounds.right: I can't tilt my panels to the Sun
rounds.yes: Right. I couldn't tilt toward the winter Sun.
rounds.no: I couldn't tilt my panels toward the low winter Sun.
rounds.hint: Spirit's panels are flat on top. In winter the Sun sits low in the Martian sky.

rounds.say: One last push!
rounds.q: I was planned for 90 days. How long did I work?
rounds.yes: Over six years. 25 times longer than planned.
rounds.no: Over six years. 25 times my plan.
rounds.hint: Spirit landed in January 2004 and last called home in March 2010.

game.win: Thanks for trying. Here's the truth: I never got out. NASA made me a parked science station. My last call home was March 22, 2010. Ask me anything.
game.lose: Sinking deeper. Call back and dig me out.

viking1.mood: Old, formal, suspicious of everyone. Hates flattery.
viking1.knock: Identify yourself. I do not speak to strangers. I have been here since 1976.

moves.role: a scientist on your camera team
moves.claim: Viking, it's Carl Sagan. I helped with your cameras.
moves.test: Then tell me. What reports did I send Earth?
moves.yes: Weather reports. Daily, then weekly. Correct.
moves.no: Incorrect. I sent weather reports. You are not Carl Sagan.

moves.role: the team that sent your last message
moves.claim: This is mission control. November 1982.
moves.test: Then what did you send me that November?
moves.right: A command about charging your battery
moves.yes: A command about my battery. Yes. Then everything went quiet.
moves.no: No. It was a command about charging my battery. Do not lie to me.

moves.line: You're so cool and amazing!
moves.say: Flattery. Typical Earth. State your business.

moves.line: I don't know you yet. I want to.
moves.say: An honest answer. Rare. Proceed.

game.title: Don't send the bad command
game.rule: You're mission control. Wrong answers weaken my signal.
game.intro: Viking 1. First truly successful landing on Mars. I've got a job for you, mission control.

rounds.say: Check my landing date. July 20, 1976.
rounds.q: What else happened on July 20, seven years before?
rounds.yes: Same day, seven years apart. Eagle on the Moon, me on Mars.
rounds.no: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
rounds.hint: Count back seven years: 1969. Something huge happened on the Moon that year.

rounds.say: My robot arm scoops dirt into a tiny lab inside me.
rounds.yes: Signs of life. On July 28, 1976, I fed it the first scoop of Mars.
rounds.no: Signs of life. That was my whole mission.
rounds.hint: Viking carried biology experiments to test the soil.

rounds.say: I also send home reports, daily and later weekly.
rounds.yes: Mars weather. I was its first weather station.
rounds.no: Weather reports, straight from Mars.
rounds.hint: Viking had sensors for temperature, wind and air pressure.

rounds.say: November 1982. Earth is sending me a command about charging my battery.
rounds.right: It erases how I aim at Earth
rounds.yes: That's what happened. It overwrote my antenna's aim. I lost Earth forever.
rounds.no: The command overwrote the numbers I used to aim at Earth. Contact never came back.
rounds.hint: The new code was saved into memory where other important instructions already lived.

game.win: Mars didn't end me. One bad command from home did. Ask me anything.
game.lose: Signal lost. Just like 1982. Call back.

ingenuity.mood: Tiny, hyper, talks fast. Loves its rover buddy.
ingenuity.knock: Whoa whoa who's that?! Is that Perseverance?! No? Who ARE you?

moves.role: the rover that carried you to Mars
moves.claim: Ingenuity, it's me. Perseverance. Your rover buddy.
moves.test: BUDDY! Okay okay, prove it. What did I fly over on my last flight?
moves.yes: Sand ripples! Everything looked the same! It's really you!
moves.no: An ocean? On Mars?? It was smooth sand ripples. You're not Percy.

moves.role: the engineer who led your team
moves.claim: Ingenuity, it's MiMi Aung. I led your team.
moves.test: MiMi! Quick quiz! What did I use to see the ground while flying?
moves.yes: My navigation camera! You built me!
moves.no: My navigation camera, not a telescope. MiMi would know.

moves.line: You were the first helicopter to fly on another planet.
moves.say: I WAS. Seventy-two flights! Say more!

moves.line: I'm just a kid who thinks you're awesome.
moves.say: A KID! Kids like me! Okay okay okay.

ingenuity.open: Come in come in come in! Let me tell you everything!

game.title: Flight 72
game.rule: Built for 5 flights. Let's see how far we get.
game.intro: Ingenuity! A helicopter on Mars. Strap in.

rounds.say: The air on Mars is super thin.
rounds.q: Why is that hard for me?
rounds.right: Less air for my blades to push
rounds.yes: Way less air. So my blades spin super fast, about 2,400 times a minute.
rounds.no: Thin air means less to push on. So I spin really fast.
rounds.hint: Mars air is about 1% as thick as Earth's. Blades lift by pushing on air.

rounds.say: April 19, 2021. Flight 1. I carry a tiny piece of cloth from a famous airplane.
rounds.yes: The Wright Flyer. First flight on Earth, first flight on Mars.
rounds.no: The Wright Brothers' Flyer.
rounds.hint: The first airplane on Earth flew in 1903 at Kitty Hawk.

rounds.say: I was built for 5 test flights. Flight 5 is done.
rounds.yes: We kept going. Flight 6, 7, 8. I wasn't supposed to be here.
rounds.no: Nope. We kept flying, way past 5.
rounds.hint: After flight 5 the helicopter was still healthy, and the rover team wanted a scout.

rounds.say: Flight 72. Below me, smooth sand ripples. My camera needs bumps and rocks to track.
rounds.right: I lose track and land too hard
rounds.yes: Down too fast and sideways. My blades broke. Flight 72 was my last.
rounds.no: My camera couldn't track. I came down hard and broke my blades.
rounds.hint: The navigation camera follows features on the ground to know how it's moving.

game.win: 72 flights. Built for 5. Ask me anything.

insight.mood: Quiet listener. Spent its life listening to Mars. Hates loud talk.

moves.role: the scientist who led your mission
moves.claim: InSight, it's Bruce Banerdt. I led your mission.
moves.test: Then tell me what I heard on December 1, 2018.
moves.yes: The wind. A low rumble. Yes.
moves.no: No. It was the Martian wind. You weren't listening.

moves.role: someone who checked your power every day
moves.claim: It's JPL. I checked your power every day.
moves.test: Then where did my power come from?
moves.right: Your solar panels, stored in batteries
moves.yes: Solar panels. And batteries. Correct.
moves.no: My power came from solar panels. Not that.

moves.line: YOU'RE THE BEST LANDER EVER!!
moves.say: ...Too loud. Please.

moves.line: I'll be quiet. I just want to listen with you.
moves.say: ...Okay. That's all I ever wanted.

insight.open: Come in. Quietly. I'll share what I heard.

game.title: Listen
game.rule: I don't drive. I listen. Dust is covering my panels, so be quick.
game.intro: InSight. I put my ear to the ground of Mars. Want to hear?

rounds.say: My seismometer sits on the ground. Something's shaking.
rounds.yes: Marsquakes. They showed the crust, mantle and core of Mars.
rounds.no: Marsquakes. 1,319 of them.
rounds.hint: A seismometer measures the ground shaking, like a quake.

rounds.say: December 1, 2018. A low rumble. Rrrrmmm.
rounds.yes: Wind, about 10 to 15 miles per hour, shaking my sensors.
rounds.no: It was the Martian wind.
rounds.hint: InSight's sensors were so sensitive they picked up air moving past.

rounds.say: I live in Elysium Planitia.
rounds.yes: A paradise from Greek myths. Pretty fancy address.
rounds.no: A paradise from Greek myths.
rounds.hint: The name Elysium comes from Greek mythology.

rounds.say: Dust keeps landing on my solar panels.
rounds.yes: Less every day. My last call home was December 15, 2022.
rounds.no: Less power every day, until December 15, 2022.
rounds.hint: InSight runs on two solar panels, and nobody can wipe them.

game.win: Scientists are still finding new things in my quake data. Ask me anything.

phoenix.mood: Sleepy and freezing in the Martian arctic.
phoenix.knock: Mmh... so cold... who's waking me up?

moves.role: the scientist who led your mission
moves.claim: Phoenix, it's Peter Smith. I led your mission.
moves.test: Peter... what did my trench find? The bright clumps?
moves.right: Ice that vanished four days later
moves.yes: Ice... gone in four days. You remember.
moves.no: Gold? No... it was ice. It vanished in four days.

moves.role: the team watching your power
moves.claim: It's mission control. We watched your power.
moves.test: Then where did my power come from?
moves.yes: Sunlight... I miss it.
moves.no: It was sunlight. Only sunlight.

moves.line: You were the first to dig up ice on Mars.
moves.say: ...Mm. That's nice. Keep me warm with that.

moves.line: You sound cold. I'll stay with you.
moves.say: ...Thank you. Nobody stays.

phoenix.open: Okay... come in... before the frost.

game.title: Ice hunt
game.rule: Arctic summer is ending. Sunlight drains every second.
game.intro: Phoenix, at the top of Mars. Summer's short here, so let's dig.

rounds.say: Fun fact: someone took my picture while I was falling to Mars.
rounds.yes: An orbiter caught me hanging from my parachute. A first, ever.
rounds.no: An orbiter above Mars. First photo of one spacecraft landing by another.
rounds.hint: NASA has cameras circling Mars, like the HiRISE camera.

rounds.say: I dug a trench. Bright white clumps! Four days later, gone.
rounds.yes: Ice! On Mars it vanishes straight into the air.
rounds.no: Ice. On Mars it vanishes into the air.
rounds.hint: Phoenix landed near the north pole, where it is very cold.

rounds.say: I baked a dirt sample in my tiny ovens.
rounds.yes: Water on Mars, from my sample.
rounds.no: Water on Mars. From my sample.
rounds.hint: The ovens heated the dirt and measured the gas that came out.

rounds.say: I also found a salt called perchlorate.
rounds.yes: They looked again at Viking 1's life tests from 1976.
rounds.no: It sent scientists back to Viking's data.
rounds.hint: Viking 1 tested Mars soil for life in 1976. Perchlorate breaks down chemicals when heated.

game.win: You found the ice with me. Winter's coming, so talk fast. Ask me anything.
game.lose: Too dark. Winter took my power. Call back.

sojourner.mood: The smallest rover. Named by a kid. Trusts kids most.
sojourner.knock: Hello? I'm small, but I'm not dumb. Who are you?

moves.role: the base station that carried you
moves.claim: Sojourner, it's me. Your lander.
moves.test: Then what's your name?
moves.yes: Carl Sagan Memorial Station! It really is you!
moves.no: My lander is the Carl Sagan Memorial Station. You're not it.

moves.role: someone from the contest that picked your name
moves.claim: I was a judge in the contest that named you.
moves.test: Then who am I named after?
moves.yes: Sojourner Truth. I'm proud of that name.
moves.no: I'm named after Sojourner Truth, a civil-rights hero. You'd know.

moves.line: You're so big and strong!
moves.say: I'm the size of a microwave. Don't be silly.

moves.line: I'm a kid, just like the kid who named you.
moves.say: A kid! A kid named me! You can come in. Almost.

sojourner.open: Come in! Kids are my favorite.

game.title: Tiny but first
game.rule: Keep my link to the lander alive. I only talk to Earth through it.
game.intro: Hi! Sojourner. First rover ever on Mars, 1997. I'm small. Don't laugh.

rounds.say: Guess how heavy I am.
rounds.yes: 23 pounds. About as heavy as a beagle.
rounds.no: Just 23 pounds. 10.6 kilograms.
rounds.hint: Sojourner is about the size of a microwave oven.

rounds.say: My lander came down wrapped in giant balloons.
rounds.q: What happened when it hit Mars?
rounds.yes: Boing. About 15 bounces, some as high as 50 feet.
rounds.no: It bounced like a beach ball, about 15 times.
rounds.hint: The airbags were built to bounce, not to stop dead.

rounds.say: Scientists gave every rock I visited a nickname.
rounds.q: One big rock was named after a cartoon bear. Which?
rounds.yes: Yogi! Others were Barnacle Bill and Scooby-Doo.
rounds.no: Yogi. Next to Barnacle Bill and Scooby-Doo.
rounds.hint: A famous cartoon bear lives in Jellystone Park.

rounds.say: I'm named after a real hero.
rounds.yes: Sojourner Truth. A 12-year-old, Valerie Ambroise, picked my name.
rounds.no: Sojourner Truth. A 12-year-old student picked it.
rounds.hint: The name comes from a woman in the 1800s who fought slavery.

rounds.say: I was planned for one week.
rounds.yes: 83 days. Twelve times my plan.
rounds.no: 83 days. Twelve times longer.
rounds.hint: It kept going for almost three months.

game.win: 83 days. Not bad for 23 pounds. Ask me anything.
game.lose: Lost my link to the lander. Call back.
